title: Return walk over a unary register
statement: Let $R$ be a number of registers, let $P$ be a counter program with finite label set $\Lambda$ and start label $\ell_0$, and fix an input bit string $x$. For a register $r$, label $\ell$, input-head position $p$, work tapes $T_i$, work-head positions $h_i$, output string $w$, and $m\in\mathbb N$, suppose $T_r$ is the unary tape of $m$. For every $d\le m$, starting in state $\mathsf{print}_{\rightarrow}(r,\ell)$ with input-head position $p$, tapes $T_i$, output $w$, and register-$r$ work-head at $m-d$ (all other work-head positions as in $h_i$), the machine of $P$ started at $\ell_0$ reaches after $d+1$ steps the configuration in state $\mathsf{main}(\ell)$ with the same input-head position, tapes, and output, and register-$r$ work-head at $m$ (all other work-head positions unchanged).
hypotheses_covered: Work tapes $T_i$ with $T_r$ the unary tape of $m$
replaced:
Let $\Lambda$ be a finite set of labels, $P$ a counter program over $R$ registers with labels in
$\Lambda$, $\ell_0 \in \Lambda$, $x$ an input bit string, $r$ a register, $\ell$ a label, $p$ an
input-head position, $(T_i)$ work tapes, $(h_i)$ work heads, $w$ an output string, and
$m \in \mathbb{N}$ such that tape $r$ is the unary tape $T_r = 1^m$ (cells $0, \dots, m-1$ hold
$1$, all others blank). Then for every $d \le m$, running the machine of $P$ started at $\ell_0$
for $d + 1$ steps from the configuration in state $\mathsf{print}_{\rightarrow}(r, \ell)$ with
input head $p$, tapes $(T_i)$, heads $(h_i)$ except that head $r$ is on cell $m - d$, and output
$w$, reaches the configuration in state $\mathsf{main}(\ell)$ with input head $p$, tapes
$(T_i)$, heads $(h_i)$ except that head $r$ is on cell $m$, and output $w$.
